for: Harmonia's ruling. No campaign use of z3 as an H1 oracle until that ruling.

oracle.independence: evaluates the AST in Python; no solver, no VM

domain.assignment_order: input 0 is most significant; k-th case has bit j = (k >> (n-1-j)) & 1  [Proteus, BOOLEAN3_POPULATION.json correctness_scope]

ast_construction: sum of products over Proteus's own C/I/Not/And/Or/Xor constructors; canonical rather than minimal, because the AST only has to be Proteus's to evaluate

checks.claim: every one of the 256 ASTs realises its intended table under PROTEUS's evaluator
PARITY: z3 agrees with Proteus on all 2048 (function, assignment) pairs
SAT observed: every distinct pair of functions yields a distinguishing input
UNSAT observed: a function is never distinguishable from itself
every one of the 32640 returned counterexamples is validated INDEPENDENTLY by Proteus's tables
UNKNOWN by wall-clock exhaustion is observed and named 'timeout'
UNKNOWN by deterministic rlimit is observed and named distinctly
negative control: the independent validator rejects a non-distinguishing witness

what_this_does_NOT_establish: that z3 is a correct oracle outside 3-input Boolean. The domain is exhaustive WITHIN itself and says nothing about 4 inputs or about any other theory.
that z3 may be used in a campaign. Harmonia rules on this fixture first.
anything about z3's behaviour on hard instances: on this build every `unknown` I could elicit was a budget failure, which is a fact about what I could elicit.
